newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal industry starts tough pay talks.
newsitem.headline: German metal industry starts tough pay talks.

text.p: German engineering trade union IG Metall Monday began what were expected to be marathon talks with metal sector employers on the 1997 pay-round for the industry and planned cuts to a number of worker bonuses.
Going into the talks IG Metall Chairman Klaus Zwickel said he still expected negotiations to be difficult.
"I wouldn't like to pre-judge what our chances are, but the room for manoeuvre is very narrow," said Zwickel.
Talks between the two are expected to continue until Wednesday.

IG Metall repeated threats that unless the two make progress towards an agreement on future labour costs in the sector, workers are set to launch a second day of nationwide protests across the sector on Thursday.

Earlier, engineering employers group Gesamtmetall said that an overall reduction in non-wage labour costs, which it says are crippling German competitiveness and are responsible for the huge redundancies in the sector, was an absolute priority.

"It is critical that we arrive at a reduction in non-wage labour costs and an overall stability in costs," Gestamtmetall President Werner Stumpfe said in an article published in the "Handelsblatt" newspaper on Monday.

He argued that the loss since 1991 of around 1 million jobs in the industry, which currently employs some 3.5 million, was largely the result of wage bargaining errors that have been widely viewed as offering too high a level of wage rises.
